judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence — 'shall be the sole remedies respecting such defect available to the Certificateholders or to the Securities Administrator on their behalf' — is a sole-remedy limitation that mixes singular obligation with plural 'remedies' and is confined to 'a defect in a constituent document', leaving open whether it reaches representation-and-warranty breaches.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It names only the Certificateholders and the Securities Administrator, yet Section 2.02(d) directs the Trustee to enforce repurchase, cure and substitution obligations 'on behalf of the Trust', so the sole-remedy limitation and the Trustee's enforcement mandate pull in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Trustee's duty extends to 'any other obligations of the related Seller or the related Originator under such agreements' — an unbounded catch-all after specific repurchase/cure/substitute duties — and the Accredited backstop is expressed as an 'including, without limitation' example rather than a separate covenant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against Section 2.02(c)'s sole-remedy sentence and against Section 2.03's repurchase paragraphs, and the obligations it tells the Trustee to enforce live in the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement and Bring Down Agreements rather than in this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section is captioned as the Master Servicer's and Securities Administrator's representations and its lettered clauses are Wells Fargo's own corporate representations, yet the unlettered paragraphs that follow impose notice, substitution and repurchase machinery on Sellers and Originators who make no representations here at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Numerous other provisions — the Mortgage Loans definition (Section 2.03(b)(v)), Substitution Adjustment Amount (Section 2.03(d)), Replacement Mortgage Loan condition (ix), Sections 2.05(a), 2.05(b), 4.02 and the Interest Funds and Principal Funds definitions — treat Section 2.03 as the source of loan-level representations and remedies, which it is not.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence survival clause; its oddity is that it makes representations survive 'delivery of the respective Mortgage Loans and Mortgage Files', language apt for loan-level warranties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The representations 'set forth in Section 2.03' are Wells Fargo's corporate representations, which have nothing to do with delivery of Mortgage Files, and the Mortgage Loans definition cites a non-existent Section 2.03(b)(v) as if this subsection contained loan-level warranties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Upon discovery by the Depositor, the Trustee of a breach' is missing a conjunction, clause (ii) is mislabelled 'Gi)', and the title representation is squeezed into an unnumbered paragraph after the enumerated corporate representations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Depositor's good-title representation survives delivery and triggers a notice duty, but no cure, repurchase or substitution remedy is provided for its breach anywhere in the Agreement, unlike the Seller and Originator representations addressed by Sections 2.02(c)–(d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'not in default or as to which default is not reasonably foreseeable' is a forward-looking, contestable standard, and the REMIC list is garbled ('REMIC I, REMIC I').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conditions repurchases and substitutions 'pursuant to Sections 2.02 or 2.03', but Section 2.03 as drafted contains no loan-level representations to be breached, so the trigger it assumes is not there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The remedy is expressed as being 'at such party's option' among cure, substitution or repurchase, while also imposing a 90-day outer limit only on limb (iii), and 'the same manner as it would a Mortgage Loan subject to repurchase' is an elliptical construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has the Securities Administrator or Custodian reconvey the loan, whereas Sections 2.02(c) and 2.03 have the Trustee or Custodian release the Mortgage File and execute the transfer instruments — different actors for the same step.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: The purposes list must accommodate Section 4.22's Supplemental Interest Trust and swap arrangements, which are not obviously within limbs (a) to (c) and depend on the breadth of the catch-alls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A very long provision mixing an absolute duty ('shall cause the Servicers to perform and observe the covenants') with broad discretion ('full power and authority to do any and all things which it may deem necessary or desirable'), and the reconciliation sentence refers back to 'the previous sentence' loosely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The absolute 'shall cause the Servicers to perform' duty here is measured in Section 4.03(b) by a much softer standard ('as the Master Servicer in its good faith business judgment would require were it the owner'), so the two sections state the same duty differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite three-limb prohibition with REMIC Opinion exceptions; the REMIC list contains the usual 'REMIC I, REMIC I' slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires the Trustee to 'comply with any directions of the Seller, the Servicers or the Master Servicer', which sits awkwardly with the Trustee's independent duties in Article X, and it treats Section 2.03 as a source of substitutions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in its judgment' and 'take such other action as it deems appropriate' leave the Master Servicer's obligation almost entirely discretionary despite the mandatory 'shall be responsible for reporting'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out '(other than Wells Fargo)' is picked up and completed by Section 4.03(b), which routes Wells Fargo's termination through the Trustee; the two subsections fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence is a double negative that is hard to apply ('Nothing herein shall impose any obligation on the part of the Trustee to assume ... unless the Trustee has not been able to find a successor servicer'), and 'Successor master Servicer' is used with irregular capitalisation for a term defined elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The enforcement standard here ('as it would were it the owner of the related Mortgage Loans') is softer than the absolute duty to 'cause the Servicers to perform' in Section 4.01, and the last sentence potentially obliges the Trustee to assume master servicing, which Section 8.06 governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully itemised reimbursement provision; 'Successor Servicer' is capitalised here though the Agreement uses 'successor servicer' elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reimbursement 'from the Distribution Account' must be squared with Sections 5.02 and 5.03, which govern permitted withdrawals from that account.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long grant of 'full power and authority to do any and all things that it may deem necessary or desirable', qualified by a REMIC proviso; the REMIC lists are garbled ('REMIC J', 'REMIC II, REMIC II') and the parenthetical '(and the Trustee shall have no liability for misuse ... by the Master Servicer, the related Servicer)' omits a conjunction.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.01 contains a parallel and differently worded access provision covering Certificateholders and the FDIC, and this one adds the OTS and other regulators, leaving two overlapping access regimes.
